# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Premera Blue Cross, Attn: Member Appeals, P.O. Box 91102, Seattle, WA 98111-9202
**Fax:** 425-918-5592

**From:** Taylor Lawson
**Member ID:** W261288012
**Member address:** [My mailing address]
**Member phone:** [My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 7, 2026 — total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) — Reference number POC-F781755028-57061**

**Governing policy:** Premera medical policy **Shoulder Arthroplasty (7.01.590)**, available at https://www.premera.com/medicalpolicies/7.01.590.pdf

---

Dear Member Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which Premera denied on August 7, 2026 as not medically necessary. I am asking Premera to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti of orthopedic surgery, has documented that this surgery is needed, and I believe the records already submitted meet the criteria in Premera's own policy, Shoulder Arthroplasty (7.01.590).

Below I set out the plan's published criteria and the matching information from my medical records.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. A documented diagnosis.** The policy states:

> "There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following: o Degenerative joint disease (DJD) o Osteoarthritis (OA) o Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) o Traumatic arthritis o Avascular necrosis"

My chart documents [the diagnosis as recorded by Dr. Marchetti — please see the office notes submitted with the prior authorization]. My shoulder radiographs of June 15, 2026 show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid, and my examination documents glenohumeral crepitus.

**2. Treatment is needed because of pain or functional disability.** The policy states:

> "Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following: o Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration o Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration"

My records document 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. They also document that I cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without help, and cannot sleep on the affected side. My examination shows active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees and external rotation limited to 10 degrees. That is well beyond the three-month duration the policy asks for, and it describes activities of daily living I cannot perform.

The policy states the same requirement again in the section addressing degenerative joint disease:

> "For a total shoulder arthroplasty and degenerative joint disease such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis or traumatic arthritis or osteonecrosis ALL of the following are present: o Needs treatment because of disabling pain and/or limited shoulder function interfering with activities of daily living (ADLs)"

**3. Imaging evidence in the 12 months before surgery.** The policy states:

> "Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following: o Irregular joint surfaces o Glenoid sclerosis o Glenoid osteophyte changes o Flattened glenoid o Cystic changes in the humeral head o Joint space narrowing"

and, in the section on degenerative joint disease:

> "Imaging evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by one or more of the following: irregular joint surfaces, glenoid sclerosis, glenoid osteophyte changes, flattened glenoid, cystic changes in the humeral head or joint space narrowing"

The policy requires **one or more** of those findings. My radiographs of June 15, 2026 — true AP and axillary views, taken within 12 months of the requested surgery — document **four**: joint space narrowing (in fact complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space), glenoid osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. A CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

**4. Three months of failed conservative management with medication.** The policy states:

> "Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following: o Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics o Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate"

My records document NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on April 28, 2026 that gave only three weeks of partial relief. That is both categories the policy lists, and the medication trial is more than twice the three months required.

**5. A six-week trial of supervised physical measures.** The policy states:

> "A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: o Physical therapy"

I completed supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening from May 3, 2026 to June 28, 2026 — eight weeks and 18 visits, longer than the six weeks the policy requires. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

The policy combines these last two requirements as well:

> "History of unsuccessful three-month trial of failed non-operative conservative management of one or more of the following medications: anti-inflammatory drugs or analgesics, or intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate, and a 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: physical therapy, or flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, or reasonable restriction of activities."

My records meet both halves of that sentence.

**6. What the records are supposed to show.** The policy states:

> "The individual's medical records submitted for review for all conditions should document that medical necessity criteria are met for the procedure requested."

I believe the records submitted with the prior authorization request do exactly that, point by point, as set out above.

## A request for clarification

The denial notice tells me the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, but it does not tell me **which** criterion Premera found was not met. I am not able to respond to a specific concern that has not been identified.

I would also note that some of the criteria in the policy introduce lists of further conditions that I do not have the full text of — for example, the policy's provision beginning "For a total shoulder arthroplasty and degenerative joint disease such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis or traumatic arthritis or osteonecrosis ALL of the following are present:" continues beyond the portion quoted above. The policy also sets out separate pathways for other conditions:

> "Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions: • Proximal humerus fracture malunion or non-union • Reconstruction after tumor resection of the glenohumeral joint or surrounding tissue • Failed hemi-arthroplasty • Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing shoulder joint destruction"

and

> "For other conditions, detailed clinical documentation supporting the diagnosis of one of the following: o Proximal humerus fracture malunion or non-union o Reconstruction after tumor resection of the glenohumeral joint or surrounding tissue o Failed hemi-arthroplasty o Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing shoulder joint destruction"

If Premera relied on a criterion I have not quoted here, I ask that the reviewer identify that criterion in writing so that I and Dr. Marchetti can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Premera to:

1. Overturn the August 7, 2026 denial and authorize total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) as requested by Dr. Marchetti;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with training in orthopedic surgery;
3. If the denial is upheld, tell me in writing the specific criterion in Shoulder Arthroplasty (7.01.590) that was not met and the specific records the reviewer found lacking, along with my rights to further review, including external review.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, by **February 3, 2027**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this letter to Premera Blue Cross, Attn: Member Appeals, P.O. Box 91102, Seattle, WA 98111-9202, or by fax to 425-918-5592. I can also be reached at the phone number above if any additional records would help, and I am glad to ask Dr. Marchetti's office to send anything further you need.

**Records I am enclosing or asking to be reviewed:**
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- Physical therapy discharge note covering May 3, 2026 to June 28, 2026 (18 visits)
- Shoulder radiograph report dated June 15, 2026 (true AP and axillary views)
- CT report
- Medication record documenting NSAID use and the corticosteroid injection of April 28, 2026
- [Any other records I am attaching]

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Taylor Lawson**
Member ID: W261288012
Reference number: POC-F781755028-57061
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]
[Date]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
